source_refs.note: Topic 22.3.1 with the book's insect data (PDF 197-198). The printed chart labels its y-axis 'Abundance (%)' while its scale and steps use counts; the original chart plots counts with the printed percentage labels, titles the y-axis 'Number of individuals' and completes the legend.

blocks.text: A bar chart displays categorical data with rectangular bars whose length or height is proportional to the value represented. It compares quantities across distinct categories, such as counts of species, experimental groups or measurements from samples. Categories go on the x-axis, values or frequencies on the y-axis, and bars may be vertical or horizontal.

items: Purpose and data: compare the abundance of five insect species; the categorical variable is species and the numerical variable is the number counted.
Axes: species on the x-axis, number of individuals on the y-axis.
Scale: the greatest value is 120 (ants), so scale the y-axis from 0 to 140 in steps of 20.
Bars: draw each bar to its value, with equal widths and even spacing.
Labels and title: title 'Insect species abundance in local forest'; x-axis 'Insect species'; y-axis 'Number of individuals'.

blocks.alt: Bar chart titled INSECT SPECIES ABUNDANCE IN LOCAL FOREST. Y-axis Number of individuals, 0 to 140 in steps of 20; x-axis Insect species. Five coloured bars: Ladybug 45 (16%), Ant 120 (41%), Butterfly 30 (10%), Bee 75 (26%), Dragonfly 20 (7%), with the percentage above each bar and a colour legend for all five species.
blocks.caption: Bar chart showing relative abundance of insect species in a local forest (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed bar chart titles its y-axis 'Abundance (%)', but the bars show counts and the book's own steps name the axis 'Number of individuals'; its legend also lists only three of the five species. The chart above uses 'Number of individuals' and a full legend.

blocks.title: Legend
blocks.text: A legend is a key on a chart, graph or map that explains the meaning of the symbols, colours, patterns or labels used, for example which colour stands for which category in a bar chart.
